title: agentctl claude status report, version 1
description: The document `agentctl claude status --json` writes to stdout. It carries no token material: the only upstream bytes it reproduces are usage response bodies, under `raw`, and those contain usage figures alone.

version.description: The report version. A consumer must refuse a version it does not know.

generated_at.description: When the report was built, RFC 3339 in UTC. Every countdown in the document is relative to this instant.

rows.description: The accounts the run displayed, in the order the table shows them. Rows hidden by default are present only when --all was given.

hidden.description: How many rows --all would have added. Zero when --all was given.

raw.description: The untouched usage response bodies, keyed by row id. Present only with --raw.

id.description: The identifier --account accepts for this row: the account UUID when it is unambiguous, `<account>/<organization>` when it is not, and the keychain service name for an item with no identity.

account_uuid.description: The Anthropic account UUID. Empty when the credential named no account.

organization_uuid.description: The organization UUID, or `_unknown-org` when the login could not name one.

kind.description: Where the credentials live, and so whether agentctl may write them. Only `owned` is ever refreshed. `foreign` is synthesized by discovery for a credential that belongs to something else — a third-party tool's keychain item, or a token in the environment — and is never recorded in the registry.

source.description: Where this row's credentials were actually read from on this pass.

state.description: The row state as a stable token. `state_label` is the same fact as a sentence and may be reworded; this may not.

state_label.description: The state as the table's State column spells it, payload included.

lock_state.description: What the namespace lock did on this pass. `busy` means another process held it past this run's deadline; `adopted` means this run took the winner's freshly written credentials instead of refreshing again; `migrated` means a Claude Code session has moved this namespace's credentials into the keychain and the item found is not one agentctl may write; `migrated_refreshed` means it is, and agentctl refreshed that keychain item in place under Claude Code's own lock protocol.

next_reset.description: The soonest window reset across this row, RFC 3339.

session_reset.description: When the five-hour session window rolls over, RFC 3339. Null when the response described no session window, or described one with no reset. Added alongside `next_reset` rather than replacing it, so version 1 still means what it meant.

weekly_reset.description: When the seven-day all-models window rolls over, RFC 3339. Null on the same terms as `session_reset`. Not the per-model weekly window, whose reset is in `windows`.

kind.description: `unknown` is a window this build does not recognise; its `label` carries the server's own kind string verbatim.

label.description: The window's display label, which is where a scoped window's scope appears.

percent.description: The percentage the server sent, clamped to 0..=100. Null when it sent something that is not a number.

percent_floor.description: `percent` floored, which is the figure the table and the web UI agree on.

is_active.description: Whether this is the window currently constraining the account.

credits.description: Extra-usage credits, from the response's `extra_usage` object alone. Present on every row, including rows that fetched nothing.

state.description: `off` means the account has credits and they are switched off; `unavailable` means the response said nothing about credits at all. The two are not interchangeable.

used_minor.description: Spend in minor units of `currency`. May be negative for a credited account.

currency.description: ISO 4217 code. Null unless the server sent a figure to denominate.

exponent.description: How many decimal places one minor unit represents.

limit_minor.description: The monthly ceiling in minor units. Null for an uncapped account.

scope.description: Credits belong to the organization, not the account: two rows in one organization report the same figure, and summing them double-counts.
